fixes.explanation: Yes, Nahum moves from the "Charging horseman, flashing sword, shining spear…" straight to "heaps of slain, mounds of corpses, dead bodies without end…" This is a heavy part of the passage. I think this one hurts.
Not quite, friend. Nahum says she "…betrays nations by her prostitution and clans by her witchcraft." Blessing is the opposite of what the verse says. Betrayal is the charge.

Not just the king, friend. The LORD says, "I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms." The audience the verse names is the nations and the kingdoms, a lot bigger than one man.

Right. All who see her "…will recoil from you and say, ‘Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?’…" Then the LORD asks, "Where can I find comforters for you?" Two questions, and the verse leaves them as questions.
The word isn't fight. The people who see her say, "Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?" The question is about grieving, not fighting.
Edom and Moab aren't named in this verse at all. Nahum says, "Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies." Those are the names to hold on to.
Persia and Media don't show up in this verse. Nahum names "Cush and Egypt…" as her boundless strength, with Put and Libya as allies. That's the crowd standing behind Thebes.
I can see why you'd think so, with all that water and all those allies. But Nahum says, "Yet she became an exile; she went into captivity." Thebes was taken, and Nahum doesn't soften it.
Right. Nahum says, "Yet she became an exile; she went into captivity." The water and the allies are named, and still that is what he says. Nahum tells it plainly.
Revenge isn't in the verse. Nahum says Nineveh will "…go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy." The word is refuge, a place to get away to.

That's the picture. Nahum says, "All your fortresses are fig trees with the first ripe figs; when shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater!" Shake the tree and the figs fall. That's how he pictures her fortresses.
The text says the opposite. Nahum says, "The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars." Not closed, wide open, and fire has consumed the bars.
That's the word. Nahum says, "The young locust strips the land and flies away." Strips is what the locust does, and then it flies away.
Nahum doesn't say they eat the walls. He says they settle on them on a cold day, and "When the sun rises, they fly away…" What happens at sunrise is that they fly away.
Settled isn't the word, friend. Nahum says, "Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them." The word is scattered, and no one is gathering them.
Weeping isn't what the verse says. Nahum says, "All who hear the news of you applaud your downfall…" The word is applaud.
Help isn't what the verse says. Nahum says, "All who hear the news of you applaud your downfall…" Applause is what the verse gives the news.
Not quite, friend. Nahum says they applaud "…for who has not experienced your constant cruelty?" The reason he gives is what they experienced.
